## Review - Level 2

_Congratulations! You've completed Level 2 and mastered intermediate GitHub collaboration! :trophy:_

<img src=https://octodex.github.com/images/welcometocat.png alt=celebrate width=300 align=right>

Here's a recap of what you learned in Level 2:

- **Issues**: You learned how to create and use issues to track work, bugs, and features.
- **Labels**: You organized issues using labels for better project management.
- **Issue References**: You connected issues to pull requests using special keywords.
- **Pull Request Reviews**: You practiced reviewing code changes and providing feedback.
- **Automation**: You experienced how GitHub automatically closes issues when referenced PRs are merged.

### You've leveled up! 🎮

You now have the skills to:
- Plan work using issues before writing code
- Organize projects with labels and issue tracking
- Create meaningful connections between issues and code changes
- Review and approve changes from collaborators
- Use GitHub's automation to streamline your workflow

### What's next?

Ready to continue your GitHub journey? Here are some ideas:

**Practice your new skills:**
1. Create more issues for improvements to your profile
2. Use different labels to categorize them
3. Practice the full workflow: issue → branch → commit → PR → review → merge

**Explore more advanced features:**
- [GitHub Projects](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/about-projects) - Visual project management boards
- [GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions) - Automate your development workflow
- [Protected branches](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches) - Require reviews before merging
- [Code owners](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners) - Automatically request reviews from specific people

**Continue learning:**
- [Take another GitHub Skills exercise](https://skills.github.com)
- [Explore GitHub's learning resources](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started)
- [Join GitHub Community Discussions](https://github.com/community)

**Share your progress:**
- We'd love to hear what you thought of this exercise [in our discussion board](https://github.com/orgs/skills/discussions/categories/introduction-to-github)
- Add a badge to your profile README showing you completed this training!

### Keep building! 🚀

Remember, the best way to learn is by doing. Start contributing to open source projects, collaborate with others, and keep practicing these GitHub workflows. You're well on your way to becoming a GitHub expert!

Thank you for completing Introduction to GitHub - Level 2! 🌟
